slides.headline: Are they arriving, or leaving forever?
The island
slides.text: Cythera, in Greek myth, is the island of Venus, goddess of love. Couples have come here on a pilgrimage of love.

slides.headline: Not yet
slides.text: On the right, a man whispers to a woman sitting on the grass. She looks down. She is not sure yet.

slides.headline: Helping hand
slides.text: A step further, another man helps his lady to her feet. She lets herself be pulled along, half willing.

slides.headline: One last look
slides.text: And then one woman turns to look back, one last time, at the place where she fell in love.

slides.headline: To the shore
slides.text: Down the hill, more couples walk toward the shore, where a golden boat waits to carry them away in the evening light.

slides.headline: The argument
slides.text: For three hundred years people have argued: are they arriving on the island, or leaving it at the end of the day?

slides.headline: A new genre
slides.text: Watteau painted it to enter the French Academy in 1717. They had to invent a new name for it: a fête galante.

slides.headline: Stay or go?
slides.text: The day of love is ending. If it were you, would you get on the boat, or stay for one more moment?
